ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram shows a power supply labeled 19 V on the left, with its negative terminal grounded; the upper and left nodes are the positive power supply node. This node is connected to the base of the first transistor, and the upper wire is connected to the collectors of the two transistors. Two NPN transistors form a Darlington connection, with the emitter of the first transistor connected to the base of the second transistor. The emitter of the second transistor is connected to the upper end of a 150 Ω resistor, the lower end of the resistor is grounded, and the resistor current is labeled I4. Reasoning: According to the specified method, the base of the first transistor is +19 V. Each base-emitter junction takes a 0.7 V voltage drop, so the emitter of the first transistor, that is, the base voltage of the second transistor, is 19 - 0.7 = 18.3 V. The emitter of the second transistor is another 0.7 V lower, therefore the voltage at the upper end of the 150 Ω resistor is 18.3 - 0.7 = 17.6 V. The lower end of the resistor is grounded, so the voltage across the resistor is 17.6 V. I4 = 17.6 / 150 A = 0.117333... A = 117.333... mA, rounded to one decimal place is 117.3 mA.

The current I\(_4\) is ______ mA. Answer with a floating-point number to one decimal place.

method.method_draft: Read the top/left node as +19 V relative to ground. Since the first transistor base is at +19 V, its emitter/second base node is 19 - 0.7 = 18.3 V. The second transistor emitter, at the top of the 150 Ω resistor where I4 flows, is another 0.7 V lower: 18.3 - 0.7 = 17.6 V. The resistor bottom is grounded, so the resistor has 17.6 V across it. Compute I4 = 17.6 / 150 A = 0.1173 A = 117.3 mA, then round to one decimal place.

planner_metadata.image_role: From the schematic, identify a 19 V supply rail feeding the base of the first NPN transistor and the tied collectors, the first emitter connected to the second base, and the second emitter connected through a 150 Ω resistor to ground. Identify I4 as the downward current through that 150 Ω emitter resistor. Note the displayed betas β=85 and β=30 but recognize they are not needed for this current under the fixed 0.7 V junction-drop assumption.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question's instruction that the circuit is in conventional flow notation and that each forward base-emitter junction voltage drop is 0.7 V; use the requested output unit of mA and one decimal place.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the silicon B-E junction approximation: each forward-biased base-emitter junction drops 0.7 V. In a Darlington emitter follower, the final emitter voltage is approximately the input/base voltage minus two B-E drops. Then apply Ohm's law to the emitter resistor: I4 = V_R / R.
